Neonatal pups, based on records from the closely related kit fox, are born at a relatively modest weight of 168 grams [Wwb = 168 grams], reflecting the altricial state typical of many canids. This high degree of sexual dimorphism in mass is thought to relate to resource competition and territorial defence strategies in the rugged Andean environments the species inhabits. This basal oxygen consumption is consistent with the energetic demands of a moderately sized, active cursorial predator that pursues small mammals and birds across a wide altitudinal gradient.

Gestation is relatively prolonged for a canid of this size, lasting 61 days [tg = 61 days] under the typical maternal body temperature of 38 °C [T = 38 °C], a duration that facilitates the advanced development of the foetal pups prior to parturition. The time since birth at puberty for females is reached at 365 days [tp = 365 days], a value recorded under the species' typical endothermic body temperature of 38 °C [T = 38 °C]. The delay of approximately one year before the onset of reproductive maturity is common among canids of this body mass, allowing juveniles to attain sufficient skeletal size and hunting proficiency before investing in their own offspring.

Longevity records for the Culpeo are modest compared to larger canids, with the maximum lifespan documented at approximately 13.1 years [am = approximately 13.1 years], measured under typical physiological conditions at a core body temperature of 38 °C [T = 38 °C].
